- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, lower forecast by 5–15% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a recent spike in price, forecast should not overshoot by more than 3–5% above the immediate prior peak; apply mean reversion if overshoot exceeds 5%.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more) and forecast is smooth, introduce slight volatility in forecast to match sentiment noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), forecast should be capped at 10–15% below recent high to avoid overcorrection.
